The review tackles some big questions about a flawed system – but leaves other issues in the ‘maybe later’ drawer

Stephen Timms would be forgiven for feeling his thunder has been stolen. The minister for social security has spent the last year reviewing personal independence payments (Pip) in light of Keir Starmer’s doomed measures last summer, but last week the Milburn review pitched a set of changes to the key disability benefit to great fanfare.

But when Timms took to the House of Commons to call for a “fundamental overhaul” of Pip on Tuesday, it was clear these were altogether bigger – and notably not explicitly cost-saving – ideas.
